source_text.body:
Build an experimental language compiler with an LLM coder
The author has Claude write the compiler and runtime for an experimental language called 5emel (about 15,000 lines of TypeScript/JavaScript and 3,000 of C), reading little of the code himself.
·
Nov 8, 2026
Done with
CL
Claude
What they did
Over a few weeks the author elicited the compiler and runtime for an experimental language, 5emel, from Claude Opus 5.5. The result is about 15,000 lines of TypeScript/JavaScript and 3,000 of C. He has read almost none of it, not even all of the roughly 1,600-line compiler, and relies on his background in programming books to steer.
How it went
A working compiler and runtime exist. As a test, an incognito Claude session was shown one function snippet and explained most of the language, though it was unsure about some parts.
Worth knowing
He says anyone recreating it from the snippet will have to fight through many of the same problems he did.
Try it yourself
with
Claude
Copy prompt
I want to build a small experimental programming language called [language name] with these core ideas: [2-3 syntax or semantic features]. Write the compiler or interpreter in [TypeScript/Python/other], plus a few example programs and a test suite that runs them. Work in small steps, run the tests after each one, and stop when all the example programs compile and run correctly. Then give me a short summary of the architecture.
Original source: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50409658
